item.description:
What's new in 3.1.0

Shepherd panes can be web browsers now — a real page beside the agent that is working on it, on this Mac or on a server. One Claude can direct others as panes of their own. A pane can be handed the last session that ran in its folder. And the Remote Panel's list of open ports has become a Security tab that will scan the box and tell you what is wrong with it.

A browser in a pane — ⌘G

  • A globe in a pane's title bar turns it into a browser and back, drawn over an agent that goes on running underneath — the third overlay a tile can wear, after Files and MCP.
  • Or open a browser as a pane of its own, from the New Panel card, beside the agents rather than over one.
  • An agent can open one itself, in a pane beside its own, and say what it wants you to look at.
  • The page is kept, not the address. Toggling back to the agent and returning lands on the same page, scrolled where you left it, with its history behind it — and a server's pane survives a reconnect the same way.
  • The pane is named after the page it is showing. A typed index.html opens as that file, and an address written without its scheme opens as https.
  • Hovering a link in a terminal now shows what it points at while you are still deciding whether to open it.

One Claude directing others — /omd

  • Type /omd in a session and it becomes a master: it plans the split, Dax draws the panes it is about to open over the right half of that tile, and you press return.
  • Each stream opens as a real Claude session in its own pane, its own git worktree and its own branch, already knowing whose it is and who to report to.
  • Nothing new is invented to carry it — herdr already splits a pane and starts an agent in it, and Claude Code already gives every session a name and a way to reach another. What was missing was the relationship, and that is what this adds.

Hand a pane the last session that ran there

  • A clock button on the tile lists every session that has run in that pane's folder, grouped by when, and one click types the chosen session's digest into the prompt.
  • Load, not copy — the clipboard never sees it, and Return is left for you to press.
  • Unlike Copy Context, the old pane does not have to still be open.

The Remote Panel's Security tab

  • Services & Ports is now Security, with that list as its first pane and a scan as its second. The list says what is on the box; the scan says whether any of it is a problem.
  • It checks the firewall, what the internet can reach, SSH, accounts, patching and hardening — in one connection — and grades the result: databases on 0.0.0.0, root login over SSH, empty passwords, extra UID 0 accounts, unattended sudo, pending security updates, world-writable files in /etc, and containers publishing past a firewall that says they can't.
  • It only reads. Every finding carries the command you would run, to copy — never a button that runs it.
  • A check it wasn't allowed to run says so rather than passing, and if too many come back that way the grade is withheld. Most of this needs root, and an A earned by not being permitted to look would be worse than no scan at all.

⌘-clicking what an agent printed

  • Foo.swift:42:8 opens at line 42, column 8 — the numbers were already being read to find where the filename ended, and then thrown away.
  • The line number lights up as part of the link rather than being left outside it.
  • A bare filename with no path is ⌘-clickable when the file is really there.

Choosing an agent

  • All nineteen descriptions are rewritten to say whose the agent is in words you have already met — Codex is "Made by OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT" — instead of naming a shape of software to people who already know the shape.
  • Each row says who makes it, and Codex is called OpenAI Codex.

Around the app

  • An upload can be called off. Hover the File Drop well while it is working and the ring becomes an ×; only the well cancels, so clicking anywhere else still opens the shelf.
  • A server connection test puts its answer over the button that asked for it.
  • The account row opens Home rather than Settings, and the annotation editor gives the keyboard back when it closes.
  • A toast about an agent on a server now asks whether Dax is connected to that machine now, not whether this window has ever visited it.
  • The Pro card no longer claims remote servers as a paid feature — it never was one, in either direction.
  • Say thanks to an agent and it says something back.
  • Signed, notarized, universal (Apple Silicon & Intel), macOS 14+.
